title: Introduction to Git Workflow
overview: Git workflow defines the process developers follow to manage code changes from development to deployment.

example.title: Basic Workflow
example.content:
Create Branch
 ↓
Write Code
 ↓
Commit Changes
 ↓
Push Code
 ↓
Merge

title: Feature Branch Workflow
overview: Feature branch workflow allows developers to create separate branches for new features.

example.title: Feature Flow
example.content:
Main Branch
 ↓
Feature Branch
 ↓
Development
 ↓
Merge

title: Git Flow Workflow
overview: Git Flow is a structured branching model that uses branches like feature, develop, release, and main.

title: Team Collaboration Workflow
overview: Teams use Git workflows to organize code reviews, changes, and releases efficiently.

example.title: Team Flow
example.content:
Developer
 ↓
Branch
 ↓
Pull Request
 ↓
Code Review
 ↓
Merge

title: Commit Best Practices
overview: Good commits should be small, meaningful, and describe the changes clearly.

example.title: Good Commit Messages
example.content:
Good:
Add user login validation

Bad:
Updated code

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned different Git workflows, branching strategies, collaboration process, and commit practices.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ Use branches for features.
✔ Review code before merging.
✔ Keep commits meaningful.
